Catalan

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): (Central, Balearic) [ˈɡo.mə]
  • IPA(key): (Valencia) [ˈɡo.ma]
  • Audio (Barcelona):(file)

Noun

[edit]

goma f (plural gomes)

  1. rubber
  2. gum
  3. eraser

Galician

[edit]
Galician Wikipedia has an article on:
goma
Wikipedia gl

Etymology

[edit]

First attested in 1350. From Late Latin gumma, from Latin cummi, from Ancient Greek κόμμι (kómmi).

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • IPA(key): /ˈɡoma/ [ˈɡo.mɐ]
  • IPA(key): (standard) /ˈɡoma/ [ˈɡo.mɐ]
  • IPA(key): (gheada) /ˈħoma/ [ˈħo.mɐ]

  • Rhymes: -oma
  • Hyphenation: go‧ma

Noun

[edit]

goma f (plural gomas)

  1. resin, sap, gum
    • c1350, K. M. Parker (ed.), Historia Troyana. Santiago: Instituto "Padre Sarmiento", page 197:
      era chẽo de dentro de moytas espeçias et de gomas as mays nobles et as mays virtuosas que ẽno mũdo auya
      it was filled in the inside with many spices and resins, the most noble and virtuous that there were in the world
  2. (uncountable) rubber (material)
  3. eraser

References

[edit]
  • “goma”, in Dicionario da Real Academia Galega (in Galician), A Coruña: Royal Galician Academy, 2012–2026
  • “goma”, in Dicionário Estraviz de galego (in Galician), 2014–2026
  • Seoane, Ernesto Xosé González; Granja, María Álvarez de la; Agrelo, Ana Isabel Boullón (2006–2022), “goma”, in Dicionario de Dicionarios do galego medieval [Dictionary of dictionaries of Medieval Galician] (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega
  • Barreiro, Xavier Varela; Guinovart, Xavier Gómez (2006–2018), “goma”, in Corpus Xelmírez: corpus lingüístico da Galicia medieval [Corpus Xelmírez: linguistic corpus of Medieval Galicia] (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega
  • Antón Luís Santamarina Fernández, editor (2006–2013), “goma”, in Dicionario de Dicionarios da lingua galega [Dictionary of Dictionaries of the Galician language] (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega
  • Antón Luís Santamarina Fernández, Ernesto Xosé González Seoane, María Álvarez de la Granja, editors (2003–2018), “goma”, in Tesouro informatizado da lingua galega (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega
  • Rosario Álvarez Blanco, editor (2014–2024), “goma”, in Tesouro do léxico patrimonial galego e portugués (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega, →ISSN

Hausa

[edit]
Hausa numbers (edit)
100
 ←  1  ←  9 10 20  →  100  → 
1
    Cardinal: gōmà

Etymology

[edit]

From Proto-Chadic *gʷam-, likely an old borrowing from Niger-Congo (compare Proto-Bantu *ìkʊ́mì), or from Proto-Afroasiatic with metathesis. If so, cognate with Egyptian mḏw and Proto-Berber *măraw (whence Central Atlas Tamazight ⵎⵔⴰⵡ (mraw)). Cognate with Ngizim gūmà, Bura kuma, Daba guɓ, Podoko jɨ́ma, Kirya-Konzel gùm, Duwai gū̀mà.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ɡóː.mà/
    • (Standard Kano Hausa) IPA(key): [ɡʷóː.mə̀]

Numeral

[edit]

gōmà f

  1. ten

Derived terms

[edit]
  • gomiya

Old English

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Proto-West Germanic *gōmō, from Proto-Germanic *gōmô.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈɡoː.mɑ/
  • Rhymes: -oː.mɑ

Noun

[edit]

gōma m

  1. palate, the roof of the mouth
    • Exeter Book, riddle 40
      Iċ eom on gōman ġēna swētra
      þonne þū bēobrēad blende mid huniġe;
      I am sweeter still in the mouth
      than when you blend bee-bread with honey
  2. jaws

Declension

[edit]

Weak:

singular plural
nominative gōma gōman
accusative gōman gōman
genitive gōman gōmena
dative gōman gōmum

Descendants

[edit]
  • Middle English: gome, goome, gomme, gumme
    • English: gum, goom (dialectal)
    • Scots: goom, geem, gum

Portuguese

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈɡõ.mɐ/
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈɡõ.mɐ/
    • (Southern Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈɡo.ma/
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /ˈɡo.mɐ/

  • Rhymes: -omɐ

Etymology 1

[edit]

Inherited from Late Latin gumma, from Latin cummi, from Ancient Greek κόμμι (kómmi).

Noun

[edit]

goma f (plural gomas)

  1. starch (laundry stiffener)
  2. gum (viscous substance exuded by certain plants)
  3. (Brazil, slang, regional) home, house
    Cola na minha goma mais tarde pra gente jogar um pouco de videogame.
    Come to my house later so we can play some video games.

  • goma-laca
  • gomar
  • gomoso

Latex being collected from a tapped rubber tree, Cameroon

Etymology 1

[edit]

Inherited from Late Latin gumma, from Latin cummi, from Ancient Greek κόμμι (kómmi).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈɡoma/ [ˈɡo.ma]
  • Audio (Costa Rica):(file)
  • Rhymes: -oma
  • Syllabification: go‧ma

Noun

[edit]

goma f (plural gomas)

  1. rubber (substance, material)
    Synonym: caucho
    1. ellipsis of cinta de goma or goma elástica (“rubber band”)
      Synonym: (Southern Cone, Puerto Rico) gomita
    2. (botany, Bolivia) rubber tree
    3. (Bolivia) teether
    4. ellipsis of goma de borrar (“eraser”)
      Synonym: borrador
    5. condom
      Synonyms: preservativo, condón
    6. tire
      1. (Rioplatense, Chile, vulgar, chiefly in the plural) boob; tit
  2. gum (substance exuded by certain plants)
    Synonym: resina
    1. (Colombia, Peru, Bolivia, Chile) ellipsis of goma de mascar (“chewing gum”)
      Synonym: chicle
    2. (Nicaragua, Costa Rica, Cuba, Andes, Guatemala, Panama, Uruguay) glue
      Synonym: pegamento

  • goma en barra (“glue stick”) (Costa Rica, Ecuador, Guatemala, Panama, Peru, Uruguay)

[edit]

See the etymology of the corresponding lemma form.

Verb

  1. inflection of gomar:

Etymology 3

[edit]

Adjective

[edit]

goma f

  1. (Bolivia, colloquial) easy (Consenting readily to sex)
  2. feminine singular of gomo

Noun

[edit]

goma f (plural gomas)

  1. feminine singular of gomo
  2. (Central America, Panama, Spain) clipping of gomona (“hangover”)
    Synonym: resaca
  3. (Spain) hair tie, ponytail holder, ponytailer, hair elastic, bobble, hair boble
    Synonyms: (Spain) goma del pelo, (Argentina, Colombia) colita, (Chile) colet, (Mexico) liga, colero
  4. (Mexico, Nicaragua, Cuba, Dominican Republic, Puerto Rico, Venezuela) home plate
  5. (Colombia, Eastern Venezuela) obsession
  6. (Peru, Chile) spanking
  7. (Bolivia) airbag
  8. (Bolivia, vulgar) A promiscuous woman.
  9. (Chile, slang) illicit pills
  10. (El Salvador) the freshness of freshly-washed clothing
  11. (Paraguay) physical discomfort

Tagalog

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Spanish goma (“rubber; gum”), from Late Latin gumma (“gum; resin”), from Latin cummi (“gum”), from Ancient Greek κόμμι (kómmi, “gum”), from Egyptian qmy (“anointing oil”), qmyt (“acanthus resin, gum”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Standard Tagalog) IPA(key): /ˈɡoma/ [ˈɡoː.mɐ]
  • Rhymes: -oma
  • Syllabification: go‧ma

Noun

[edit]

goma (Baybayin spelling ᜄᜓᜋ)

  1. rubber; gum
    Synonyms: kola, pangkola
  2. rubber band; elastic band
    Synonym: lastiko
  3. rubber eraser
    Synonym: pambura
  4. rubber tire
  5. rubber shoes

Derived terms

[edit]
  • gomahan

Adjective

[edit]

goma (Baybayin spelling ᜄᜓᜋ)

  1. made of rubber

[edit]

  • “goma”, in Pambansang Diksiyonaryo | Diksiyonaryo.ph, 2018
